# Berkeley — Three Dialogues (1734 text, Wilkins ed. 2002)

## Essay use

A fixed public carrier for one historical immaterialist formulation and its immediate intratextual objection. It can place M47’s idealist horizon in a real philosophical controversy.

**Claim boundary:** Berkeley does not establish Kashmir Śaivism, QL, AI subjectivity, cosmology, or an inference from engineered systems to idealism.

## Passage preparation

Exact text, fixed edition, speaker context, and limitation: [Quotes — Berkeley Three Dialogues (Wilkins, 2002)](#passages).

<a id="berkeley-1734-three-dialogues-wilkins-2002-q001"></a>
## Passage card — `berkeley-1734-three-dialogues-wilkins-2002-q001` — Philonous’s conditional immaterialist formulation
^berkeley-1734-three-dialogues-wilkins-2002-q001

> “That there is no such Thing as what Philosophers call Material Substance, I am seriously persuaded: But if I were made to see any thing absurd or sceptical in this, I should then have the same Reason to renounce this, that I imagine I have now to reject the contrary Opinion.”

- **Locator:** First Dialogue, printed p. 1; Wilkins PDF p. 8/69 (index 7); speaker Philonous.
- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent and coordinator, 2026-07-14; manually transcribed and checked against typeset PDF/speaker context; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted primary philosophy.
- **Evidential action:** contextualises/supports.
- **Argument function:** historical idealist formulation with self-limit.
- **Consumers:** [[47-s50-p4-idealism-horizon]]; [[section-rooms/arguments/A26-Objective-Internality-Mind-as-Worldhood|Agent Subjectivity Must Remain Open]].
- **Use boundary:** establishes one historical immaterialist formulation; it does not establish QL, Śaivism, agent subjectivity, cosmology, or an engineering-to-idealism inference.

<a id="berkeley-1734-three-dialogues-wilkins-2002-q002"></a>
## Passage card — `berkeley-1734-three-dialogues-wilkins-2002-q002` — Hylas’s immediate objection
^berkeley-1734-three-dialogues-wilkins-2002-q002

> “What! can any Thing be more fantastical, more repugnant to common Sense, or a more manifest Piece of Scepticism, than to believe there is no such Thing as Matter?”

- **Locator:** First Dialogue, printed p. 1; Wilkins PDF p. 8/69 (index 7); speaker Hylas.
- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent and coordinator, 2026-07-14; manually transcribed and checked against typeset PDF/speaker context; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted primary philosophy.
- **Evidential action:** qualifies.
- **Argument function:** intratextual counterposition.
- **Consumers:** [[47-s50-p4-idealism-horizon]]; [[section-rooms/arguments/A26-Objective-Internality-Mind-as-Worldhood|Agent Subjectivity Must Remain Open]].
- **Use boundary:** records a dramatic objection in Berkeley’s dialogue; it is not a validated contemporary physicalist refutation.
